title: She trained in Kerala and Bangalore before building a career in Australian child psychiatry. In 2026, the King honoured her for it.

sources.text: Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia - 2026 King's Birthday Honours List
IANS - 10 Indian-origin Australians recognised in 2026 King's Birthday Honours List

caption:
She trained in Kerala and Bangalore before building a career in Australian child psychiatry. In 2026, the King honoured her for it.

The Governor-General's official list, issued June 8, 2026, recognized her work in psychiatry, child and adolescent mental health, neurodevelopmental research and tertiary education - one of ten Indian-origin Australians honoured that year.

She now holds the chair of infant, child and adolescent psychiatry at UNSW Sydney, where her research into neurodevelopmental conditions like Tourette Syndrome and autism has produced a quality-of-life scale adopted by teams in 32 countries.

Eapen's path from Kerala's medical colleges to an Officer of the Order of Australia shows Indian psychiatric training compounding into research that's now used far beyond either country.
